cap_reasons.fish_trawl_permanent: only one gear is banned: outcomes must be shown first
cap_reasons.hunting_stable_imadas: a whole administrative sector with villages and farmland
cap_reasons.military_buffer: security zone renewed yearly; consent unlikely in the short term

measures.label: No-fishing zone
measures.authority: Direction Générale de la Pêche et de l'Aquaculture (DGPA, Ministry of Agriculture); Coast Guard for enforcement
measures.measure: All fishing is banned all year (fishing order of 28/09/1995, art. 25).
measures.values: Refuge for fish stocks next to fishing grounds (spill-over).
measures.risks: Check that the 1995 text is still in force and enforced; most of the island zones already lie inside the national park.
measures.evidence: Enforcement records, fish biomass or visual census inside vs outside.
measures.next: DGPA: confirm the text in force; report the part outside the park as an OECM, or extend the park boundary.

measures.label: Permanent trawling ban
measures.authority: DGPA (Ministry of Agriculture); GFCM (FAO) for the deep-sea FRA; National Guard maritime units
measures.measure: Bottom trawling is banned all year; other gears (nets, lines, traps) remain allowed.
measures.values: Protects seagrass meadows (Posidonia, Cymodocea) and nursery grounds that support small-scale fisheries.
measures.risks: Illegal trawling in shallow waters is widely reported (Gulf of Gabès); only one pressure is removed, so outcomes must be shown, not assumed.
measures.evidence: VMS/AIS or patrol data on trawling inside the zone; seagrass extent and condition; INSTM survey data.
measures.next: DGPA and INSTM: compile enforcement and habitat evidence; discuss with the CBD focal point whether to report as an OECM.

measures.label: Seasonal trawling closure
measures.measure: Bottom trawling is banned for part of the year only.
measures.values: Lets juvenile shrimp and fish grow during the closure.
measures.risks: A seasonal closure does not give year-round, long-term protection: it rarely meets the OECM criteria on its own.
measures.next: Keep as context for the permanent zones.

measures.label: Red-coral harvesting ban
measures.measure: Only red-coral harvesting is banned; other uses continue.
measures.risks: Single-gear measure: biodiversity outcomes are unlikely to be demonstrable.
measures.evidence: Check whether other restrictions apply locally.

measures.label: Marine protected area zone not counted
measures.authority: APAL (Agence de Protection et d'Aménagement du Littoral) / Ministry of Environment; DGF for national parks
measures.measure: Marine park or reserve zone recorded by ProtectedSeas, missing from the WDPA records counted in 3.1.
measures.values: Island and coastal marine habitats managed for conservation.
measures.risks: Probably a protected area rather than an OECM: the fix is to report it to the WDPA.
measures.evidence: Legal text and boundary of the marine zone.
measures.next: Ministry of Environment / APAL: submit the zone to the WDPA through UNEP-WCMC (quickest gain, no new measure).

measures.label: Border buffer zone
measures.authority: Ministry of National Defence; governors (entry permits)
measures.measure: Closed military zone since 2013 (arrêté républicain 2013-230, renewed yearly): entry needs the governor's authorisation.
measures.risks: Security measure renewed every year, not designed for conservation; consent of the Ministry of Defence is unlikely in the short term; the mapped extent is rebuilt from text.
measures.evidence: Ungulate and bustard surveys, hunting/poaching pressure, consent of the Ministry of Defence.
measures.next: Discuss informally with the Ministry of Defence; meanwhile keep as context.

measures.label: Military area
measures.measure: Restricted access to the public over long periods; IUCN lists military lands among potential OECMs.
measures.risks: Many military sites are built-up bases or airfields; consent of the Ministry of Defence is needed; data cannot always be shared.
measures.evidence: Habitat condition inside the fence (imagery), consent, management practices (fire, grazing).
measures.next: Ministry of Defence: consent and a short habitat check of the undeveloped part.

measures.label: Hunting reserve on a named site (every season)
measures.authority: Direction Générale des Forêts (DGF, Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional forest district (CRDA)
measures.measure: Hunting banned on the same named forest, wetland or dam in every recent hunting order (art. 12).
measures.values: Game and waterbird refuge; often state forest under the Forest Code.
measures.risks: The order is renewed every season, so permanence rests on practice; only hunting is banned; the extent of the named area is approximate.
measures.evidence: Hunting orders over 10+ years, DGF management plan of the forest or dam, waterbird counts.
measures.next: DGF: confirm the reserve is permanent in practice and map its legal limits; consider a permanent status.

measures.label: Hunting reserve on a whole imada (every season)
measures.authority: DGF and the regional forest district (CRDA)
measures.measure: Hunting banned in the whole administrative sector (imada) in every recent hunting order.
measures.values: Game refuge over a mixed landscape.
measures.risks: The imada includes villages and farmland; only hunting is banned. As a whole it is unlikely to qualify; the natural habitat inside it may.
measures.evidence: Map the forest and rangeland inside the imada; check what else is managed there.
measures.next: DGF: narrow the reserve to its natural habitat (forest, rangeland) before any OECM discussion.

measures.label: Rotating or new hunting reserve
measures.measure: Hunting banned for this season only (rotating rest area for game).
measures.risks: Temporary: does not meet the long-term criterion.

measures.label: Water Code protection zone
measures.authority: DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture, dams) and SONEDE (drinking water); CRDA
measures.measure: Water Code art. 123: polluting activities banned in the immediate (10 m) and easement (10-60 m) belts around drinking-water reservoirs.
measures.values: Drinking-water security; riparian vegetation along the reservoir shore.
measures.risks: Narrow belts; the law protects water quality, not biodiversity, so habitat outcomes must be shown; the mapped belt follows the reservoir outline, not the highest-water mark.
measures.evidence: Decree listing the protected reservoirs, enforcement, vegetation of the belt.
measures.next: DGBGTH / SONEDE: confirm the list of protected reservoirs and how the belt is managed.

measures.label: Dam reservoir or hill lake
measures.authority: DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA)
measures.measure: State-owned reservoir managed for water supply and irrigation; fishing and access are regulated.
measures.values: Water supply; open water for wintering and breeding waterbirds.
measures.risks: Managed for water, not biodiversity: water-level changes and fishing; outcomes must be shown with waterbird data.
measures.evidence: International Waterbird Census counts (AAO/BirdLife Tunisia, DGF), water-level regime, fishing concessions.
measures.next: DGBGTH and DGF: compile waterbird counts and agree management of the shores (grazing, disturbance).

measures.label: Traditional oasis
measures.authority: Regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA) and oasis water-user groups (GDA); GIAHS team for Gafsa
measures.measure: Agricultural safeguard zone (Law 83-87): any change of land use needs the Minister of Agriculture's authorisation.
measures.values: Three-storey agro-ecosystem (palms, fruit trees, crops), old date varieties, traditional water sharing; cultural landscape.
measures.risks: A farmed system: OECM status rests on the agro-biodiversity it keeps and on traditional management; groundwater decline and urban spread are the main threats.
measures.evidence: Inventory of date varieties and associated species, water management by the GDA, trends in palm-grove extent.
measures.next: CRDA and the GDAs: document agro-biodiversity and governance; start with the GIAHS oasis of Gafsa.

measures.label: Modern date-palm plantation
measures.measure: Regular layout suggests a modern monoculture.

measures.label: Possible sacred grove
measures.authority: Local community and the shrine's custodians; Ministry of Religious Affairs; DGF where the trees are forest
measures.measure: Trees around a saint's shrine, traditionally not cut.
measures.values: Spiritual and cultural value; relict trees and old-growth habitat.
measures.risks: Low confidence: about 1 patch in 3 looked like a natural grove on imagery, the others were orchards; very small.
measures.evidence: Imagery or field check of the patch, custodians' rules, community consent.
measures.next: Check on imagery; if natural, document the customary rules with the community.

measures.label: Cemetery
measures.evidence: Vegetation cover; only wooded ones are worth assessing.
measures.next: Only the wooded ones, with the municipality.

measures.label: Archaeological site
measures.authority: Institut National du Patrimoine (INP) and AMVPPC (site management)
measures.measure: Heritage Code (Law 94-35): construction, digging and changes need INP approval; listed sites have a protection perimeter.
measures.risks: Managed for heritage, not biodiversity: vegetation clearance for visitors is common; mapped outlines (OSM) may not match the legal perimeter.
measures.evidence: Legal perimeter, vegetation condition (garrigue, old olive groves), INP management plan.
measures.next: INP / AMVPPC: official perimeter and vegetation management; pair biodiversity surveys with heritage monitoring.

measures.label: Cultural or historic site
measures.evidence: Only large sites with natural surroundings.

note: Screening figures: candidates from the OECM Harvester; counted PAs and KBAs from the indicator 3.1 analysis (full resolution, Mollweide); land cover from ESA WorldCover 2021. Scores and priorities are a provisional rubric to open the discussion with the administrations, not an OECM assessment.

recommendations.heading: First: report the marine zones that are already protected
recommendations.text: 2 marine park and reserve zones (Parc National de Zembra et Zembretta - zone C, Transition and sustainable development area, Iles Kneiss) are recorded by ProtectedSeas but are missing from the WDPA records counted in indicator 3.1. Reporting them through UNEP-WCMC adds 117 km² of sea with no new measure: the quickest gain.

recommendations.heading: Assess the 9 priority-1 complexes now
recommendations.text: They combine a permanent legal restriction, natural habitat and a Key Biodiversity Area: Sidi el Barrak dam, Ben Metir dam, No-fishing zone around La Galite and Galiton (1.5 mile), El Masri dam, El Ougla dam, Bezirk dam. Most are dam reservoirs whose shores are KBAs for waterbirds or freshwater species, where the Water Code belts and the hunting bans already stack. Together they add little area (13 km² on land, 122 km² at sea) but 120 km² of KBA not covered today. They are the best pilots for the national OECM recognition process.

recommendations.heading: At sea, the permanent trawling bans decide the 30% target
recommendations.text: Sea coverage is 1.07% today. The permanent bottom-trawling bans (Gulf of Gabès and Gulf of Tunis under 50 m, the 3-mile coastal band) and the deep-sea GFCM restricted area would, if recognised, take it to about 34%. They are priority 2 because only one gear is banned: Tunisia would have to show that seagrass meadows and fish nurseries are actually protected, and that illegal trawling is controlled.

recommendations.heading: On land, these categories will not close the gap
recommendations.text: Land coverage is 7.93%, 34,340 km² short of 30%. Priority 1 and 2 complexes add 1,662 km² (+1.07 points). The large areas (hunting imadas, the southern border zone) are priority 3: temporary, not designed for biodiversity, or a security zone. The land gap needs new protected areas and other OECM types not mapped here: state forests under management plans, rangeland reserves, community-managed areas.

recommendations.heading: Use OECMs to close KBA gaps where they fit
recommendations.text: 70 of the 71 KBAs are not fully covered. Priority 1 and 2 complexes reach 42 of them (most at sea and at dams), and close at least half of the gap in 13. 23 KBAs are reached by no candidate at all, including Sebkhet Sidi El Hani, Jbil, Sebkhet Kelbia, Garaet Mabtouh: they need protected areas or other measures.

recommendations.heading: Small sites with high value: sacred groves and archaeological sites
recommendations.text: Several wooded shrines in the Mogods and Kroumirie (Béja, Bizerte) lie in KBAs and score high, but the grove outlines are low-confidence detections: check them on imagery and with the communities before going further. Archaeological sites with natural vegetation (e.g. Henchir Bourgou on Djerba) are permanent and managed by the INP: biodiversity monitoring can be added to heritage management.
